review_notes: I read the whole file and the supporting lemmas manuscript_weightedComplexLogRat_interval, manuscript_interval_abs_sub_le_rounded_width and manuscript_rounded_weighted_complex_log_error_le. findings.problem: Each of the 13 composition-error lemmas re-proves the interval-membership fact that the earlier private lemma `manuscriptNormV8_k SubstituteRat_interval` already proves. The `simpa only [...]` call and the long `manuscript_weightedComplexLogRat_interval` call with all six numerals are copied. The `h`/`hw`/`simpa only [hw]` skeleton is then repeated 13 times. The width-equation step also restates both rounded endpoints a second time, once as the `h` arguments and once inside `hw`. This is the same reasoning as the `_interval` lemmas at lines 19-22 and the Group034-038 `_rounded_endpoints` statements, and it appears 13 times.
findings.proposed_change:
1. Replace each `hq` block with `have hq := manuscriptNormV8_kSubstituteRat_interval`. This is a one-line, identical-statement reuse. The private `_interval` lemmas are in an earlier `section` of the same namespace and file, so they are visible.
2. Add one shared lemma:
`theorem manuscript_abs_sub_le_of_rounded_interval (a b q lo hi w : ℚ) (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (a:ℝ) (b:ℝ)) (hq : q ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hlo : lo ≤ a) (hhi : b ≤ hi) (hw : hi - lo = w) : |x - (q:ℝ)| ≤ (w:ℝ)`.
Proof sketch: `subst hw; exact manuscript_interval_abs_sub_le_rounded_width a b q lo hi x hx hq hlo hhi`.

Each composition-error lemma then becomes `manuscript_abs_sub_le_of_rounded_interval _ _ _ _ _ _ _ manuscriptNormV8_kTerm_exact_interval manuscriptNormV8_kSubstituteRat_interval manuscriptNormV8_k_rounded_endpoints.1 manuscriptNormV8_k_rounded_endpoints.2 (by norm_num)`. The `hw` equation is the only numeric fact left, and it is discharged in the `by norm_num` argument.
   The hypotheses and imports are unchanged: only `manuscript_interval_abs_sub_le_rounded_width` from ManuscriptCaseOneX4PointRounding is used, and that file is already imported.
findings.benefit: This removes the second copy of the interval proof and the large duplicated numerals, so each lemma shrinks from about 10 lines to 2-3. A reader can see that all 13 lemmas use the same argument, and a change to the argument is made in one place. The risk that one of the 13 hand-copied six-argument calls drifts from its `SubstituteRat` definition drops.

findings.problem: Both theorems prove the same fact: thirteen termwise `|a_i - b_i| ≤ e_i` bounds give a bound on the difference of the sums. Each does it by `abs_le.mpr`, `constructor`, and then two `linarith only` calls that list all 13 `(abs_le.mp h_i).1` / `.2` terms. The `h0 … h12` / `push_cast` / `unfold` scaffolding is also copied. The same shape recurs in lines 612-657, and presumably in the other row files.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove one general lemma, for example `theorem abs_sub_sum_le_sum_of_forall {ι} (s : Finset ι) (f g e : ι → ℝ) (h : ∀ i ∈ s, |f i - g i| ≤ e i) : |∑ i ∈ s, f i - ∑ i ∈ s, g i| ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, e i`.
Proof sketch: `rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]; exact (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (Finset.sum_le_sum h)`. A list version is equally easy.
If the row sums keep their explicit 13-summand form, a binary lemma `|a-b| ≤ e → |c-d| ≤ f → |(a+c)-(b+d)| ≤ e+f` can be folded 12 times to the same effect.
Both row theorems then reduce to instantiating the lemma with the 13 per-term bounds, followed by one `norm_num`/`linarith` step that compares the total with the stated constant. The first theorem keeps its `change` to the nested-`+` form of `manuscriptNormLogRow`.
findings.benefit: This replaces about 100 lines of duplicated 13-way `abs_le`/`linarith` bookkeeping with one reusable fact and two short applications. The aggregation logic is stated once, and adding a term no longer needs edits to 26 `linarith` hypothesis lists. Changing the summand count only changes the explicit list of bounds.

findings.problem: Each of the 13 lemmas has the same three-step proof: instantiate `manuscript_rounded_weighted_complex_log_error_le` at the same six numerals that appear in the `def` just above, prove `|c| + |d| = W` by `norm_num`, then `rw [hw] at h; exact h`. The numerals `c`, `d`, `m`, `k`, `y`, `t` are retyped in the lemma statement, the `have h`, and the `hw`, in addition to the `def`. The `(by norm_num) (by norm_num)` side goals `|(m:ℝ)| ≤ 100` and `|(k:ℝ)| ≤ 4` are identical in kind every time. Only the numerals differ.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a small lemma that carries the weight-equation step:
`theorem manuscript_rounded_substitute_error_of_weight (c d : ℚ) (m k : ℤ) (y t W : ℚ) (hm : |(m:ℝ)| ≤ 100) (hk : |(k:ℝ)| ≤ 4) (hW : |(c:ℝ)| + |(d:ℝ)| = (W:ℝ)) : |(barrierWeightedComplexLogRat c d m k y t : ℝ) - (manuscriptRoundedWeightedComplexLogRat c d m k y t : ℝ)| ≤ (W:ℝ) * (3636 * manuscriptTermRoundStep)`.
Proof sketch: `hW ▸ manuscript_rounded_weighted_complex_log_error_le c d m k y t hm hk`.
Then state each per-term lemma with the `def`s unfolded, e.g. `by unfold manuscriptNormV8_0SubstituteRat manuscriptNormV8_0RoundedSubstituteRat; exact manuscript_rounded_substitute_error_of_weight _ _ _ _ _ _ (93520547693257/2000000000000000) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)`. The six numerals no longer need to be repeated.
This only needs the same imports as before.
findings.benefit: This removes the repeated six-argument instantiation and the `rw`/`exact` plumbing. The only data each term supplies is the weight constant. That makes it easy to see that all 13 lemmas are one argument, and it removes the risk of mismatched copied numerals.
